criterion: A rule ships only when one trigger of it is recorded where a test replays it: a frozen oracle that names the rule in an observed position, or a named test that scans a fixture and asserts the finding. The record proves the rule fires on the pattern it claims to catch. Precision on the corpus answers the opposite question, how often the rule is wrong on healthy code, and says nothing when the corpus never triggers it. `catches` states that pattern in one line, and for a Clippy rule it is the description the toolchain publishes, so a lint whose meaning shifts upstream stops matching its own contract.
